correctness.rationale: Writing opposite-pair means A,B and half-differences u,v gives φ=B−A. Direct addition in the original ODE gives u'=−2 cos v cos(φ+α) sin u, v'=−2 cos u cos(α−φ) sin v and φ'=−4 cos α cos u cos v sin φ. Consequently N=sin u sin v and D=sin φ solve the same multiplicative equation with coefficient −4 cos α cos u cos v cos φ, including N=0. A single 2π lift change flips both signs; D≠0 is invariant and J=N/D is genuinely defined there on the torus. At quadrature φ is fixed and p=N is a Hamiltonian of the shape system up to the constant factor 2 sin φ. On each sign cell, log|sin u|+log|sin v| is strictly concave with a unique maximum, so a regular product level is a smooth compact oval, and the field has no zeros on it. For x=|sin u|, x'²=4 sin²φ (1−x²)(x²−p²), with four monotone arcs per circuit. Substituting x²=p²+(1−p²)sin²η yields the asserted complete elliptic integral and AGM form. The pointwise primitive A−cot φ log|sin u| is constant, as is B−A, so all four real lifts return exactly. A torus return would force the changes in u,v to be integer multiples of π; since each stays within a single open semicircle, both changes must vanish, establishing minimality. Strict monotonicity and the two limits follow from K; |p|=1 is fixed and the zero-product level is singular, not a regular periodic oval.
